- VC-29: FAIL (suggestion) — SQL Lens rewrites every query so it can read only the selected set's tables and columns, and a query reaching for anything else is refused before it runs. [docs/external/rule-sets.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Traced `SELECT email FROM customers` (customers listed, email unlisted) through RuleSetGuardRunner.run_sql (src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:357-374). _rewrite -> apply_rule_set parses it, _analyze finds the listed table, and _derived (192-215) wraps it as a derived table selecting only the listed columns. Nothing in the guard checks the column names the model wrote. Only table-level refusals exist (_check_reference, 131-150). The rewritten SQL goes to self._inner.run_sql (372-374) and reaches MySQL, which fails it as an unknown column. The module docstring (17-19) says this: 'MySQL then resolves every column ... a column the set does not list fails as an unknown column'. docs/external/rule-sets.md:119 says the same: 'a column the set does not list is simply not visible ... MySQL reports it as an unknown column.' So the sentence at rule-sets.md:95 is wrong for columns, because an unlisted column is not refused before the query runs. The query is sent to MySQL, which rejects it. The tables-and-columns restriction itself holds, since the rewrite exposes only listed columns. Only the claim that every such reach is refused before running is false. The doc's own line 119 contradicts it, and refusal before running holds only for the table-level cases at lines ~110-117.

  </details>

</details>
